desc:
A day lasts from time 0 to eventTime. There are n meetings; meeting i occupies the half-open range [startTime[i], endTime[i]). The meetings are given in order, never overlap, and may touch.

You may reschedule at most k meetings. A rescheduled meeting keeps its duration and must stay within the day, the meetings must still not overlap, and the relative order of all meetings must not change. Other meetings stay where they are.

Return the maximum possible length of a continuous stretch of time in which no meeting takes place.

eventTime = 10, k = 1, startTime = [0, 2, 9], endTime = [1, 3, 10]  ->  7

Move the meeting [2, 3) to [1, 2); the stretch [2, 9) is then free.
constraints: 0 ≤ startTime[i] < endTime[i] ≤ startTime[i+1] (for consecutive meetings), and endTime[n-1] ≤ eventTime
hints: Look at the free gaps: before the first meeting, between consecutive meetings, and after the last one. There are n + 1 of them.
Pushing a meeting to one side merges the two gaps next to it. Moving several neighbouring meetings merges even more gaps, while the total free time never changes.
Moving k meetings can merge k + 1 consecutive gaps into one stretch. The answer is the largest sum of k + 1 consecutive gaps; use a sliding window.
editorial: Write gap[0] for the time before meeting 0, gap[i] for the time between meeting i-1 and meeting i, and gap[n] for the time after the last meeting. Because the order of meetings is kept, a free stretch in the final schedule is made of consecutive original gaps whose separating meetings were all pushed out of the way. Sliding j consecutive meetings to one side removes them from the middle of the stretch and merges the j + 1 gaps around them, with total length equal to the sum of those gaps (meeting durations are preserved, so free time is only redistributed).

With at most k moved meetings you can merge at most k + 1 consecutive gaps, and any such window is achievable by pushing the meetings between them to the left end and the right end of the window. The answer is therefore the maximum sum over all windows of min(k + 1, n + 1) consecutive gaps, found in O(n) with a running window sum. Space is O(n) for the gaps (O(1) is possible).
solution:
def maxFreeStretch(eventTime, k, startTime, endTime):
    gaps = []
    prev = 0
    for s, e in zip(startTime, endTime):
        gaps.append(s - prev)
        prev = e
    gaps.append(eventTime - prev)
    w = min(k + 1, len(gaps))
    cur = sum(gaps[:w])
    best = cur
    for i in range(w, len(gaps)):
        cur += gaps[i] - gaps[i - w]
        if cur > best:
            best = cur
    return best
